styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Medina lanes, the Bardo mosaics and Sidi Bou Saïd.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Roman Carthage, Punic ruins and the old medina.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Couscous, brik, fish and mint tea in the medina.

stays.why: Sleep inside the old city walls: souks, mosques and cafés on your doorstep. Quiet at night, but lanes are confusing after dark.
Central and easy: the TGM train, metro hubs and the main avenue. Best base for first-timers without a car.
Seaside suburb with cafés and a beach; TGM train to the centre in about 30 minutes.
Blue-and-white village on the cliff. Romantic and pricey; good for one or two nights, not for every day.

food: Try Tunisian staples: couscous on Friday, brik (fried pastry with egg), lablabi soup and harissa with everything.
In the medina, look for small family restaurants near the souks; a full lunch often costs 10–25 TND.
Seafood is best near La Goulette and La Marsa; grilled fish is sold by weight, so ask the price first.
Street snacks: fricassé sandwiches, makroudh pastries and mint tea in a café. Cheap and filling.
Alcohol is limited outside hotels and a few licensed restaurants. Don't count on wine with dinner everywhere.
more_time: Add a half-day at Carthage and the Bardo Museum; both need more time than most day plans allow.
Take the TGM to Sidi Bou Saïd for a slow afternoon of cafés and views over the bay.
With a spare day, head to Dougga or Kairouan by organised tour; check departure times the day before.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the medina, the Bardo and Carthage; add a night for a slow Sidi Bou Saïd and La Marsa day.

month_notes: January: cool and damp, highs near 16°C. Pack a jacket and an umbrella.
February: still cool at 17°C with about 7 rain days. Good for museums.
March: mild at 19°C but the wettest month, around 9 rain days.
April: pleasant at 22°C and drier. A strong month for walking the medina.
May: warm at 26°C with about 6 rain days. Good for sights and the coast.
June: hot at 32°C and mostly dry. Sightsee early morning and late afternoon.
July: very hot, 35°C highs and no rain. Stay hydrated and avoid midday sun.
August: as hot as July, around 35°C, with a few rain days. Evenings are best.
September: still hot at 31°C but cooling. Sea is warm for swimming.
October: comfortable at 27°C with about 7 rain days. One of the best months.
November: cooler at 21°C but wet, around 9 rain days. Bring a rain layer.
December: cool at 18°C with about 8 rain days. Quiet season, short days.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean climate: hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters. Spring and autumn are the sweet spots.

items.title: Best time: April to June and September to October
items.text: Warm days around 22–31°C with fewer rain days. Ideal for the medina, Carthage and the coast.

items.title: Summer is very hot (July to August)
items.text: Highs near 35°C and almost no rain. Plan indoor sights at midday and go out early or late.

items.title: Wettest in November and March
items.text: About 9 rain days each. Showers are usually short; carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Cool winters
items.text: January and February highs near 16–17°C and lows around 8°C. Bring a warm layer for evenings.

items.title: Sea swimming
items.text: Best from June to September when the water warms up. May and October are bracing but possible.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes and sun protection for summer; a jacket and rain layer for winter. Modest dress for mosques and the medina.

transit.best: The TGM train for the coast and metered taxis for everything else.

modes.text: Light metro with five Transtu lines, 0.500–0.650 DT per ride. Hubs at Place de la République and Place de Barcelone.
TGM from Tunis Marine to La Goulette, Carthage, Sidi Bou Saïd and La Marsa, about 0.800 DT each way. RFR lines A, D and E serve suburbs for about 1 DT; line D reaches the Bardo Museum.
Cheap, from about 0.320 DT. Airport bus 104 to Tunis Marine costs 1 DT.
Plentiful and metered. Insist on the meter, avoid hotel queues, and use the inDrive app (Bolt no longer works).
For confident drivers only. Traffic is heavy and night driving is riskier.
Best inside the medina and Ville Nouvelle. Lanes are narrow and uneven; wear good shoes.
